description: Scorpio zodiac sign: personality traits, strengths and challenges, love, career, decans and dates (October 23 to November 21).
answer: In Western astrology, Scorpio is the eighth sign of the zodiac, a fixed water sign ruled by Pluto. It is traditionally associated with intensity, loyalty, perception and emotional depth. The Sun is in Scorpio from about October 23 to November 21. The exact dates shift by a day from year to year.

sections.heading: Scorpio personality traits
paragraphs: Scorpio carries more symbols than most signs. The scorpion is the familiar one, a creature that keeps low, watches and strikes only when it has to. Older traditions add the eagle, which sees from great height, and the phoenix, which burns and rises again. Together they suggest a personality that moves through stages, from self-protection towards clear sight and renewal. People with a Scorpio Sun are often described as private, magnetic and difficult to fool. They tend to notice motives before words, and they would rather have one real conversation than a dozen polite ones.

In astrology Scorpio is a fixed water sign ruled by Pluto, with Mars, its traditional ruler, still part of the picture. Water signs process life through feeling and memory, and fixed signs hold steady once committed, so Scorpio's emotions are usually deep, lasting and kept under the surface like a still pond with a strong current. Pluto is associated with power, hidden things and transformation, which is why Scorpio is linked with crises, secrets, inheritance and reinvention. Mars lends grit and the readiness to fight for what matters. The overall portrait is someone who feels strongly, guards carefully and changes completely when change finally comes.

sections.heading: Scorpio strengths and challenges
paragraphs: Scorpio's loyalty is the real thing. Once it decides you are its person, it tends to stay through illness, failure and the parts of life most friends politely avoid. It is perceptive, often reading what is unsaid in a meeting or a family, and it is usually not frightened by grief, anger or taboo subjects. That makes it a steady presence in a crisis. Scorpio also has formidable focus: given a mystery, a problem or a goal it cares about, it can dig further and hold on longer than almost anyone. Add resourcefulness and a dry, dark humour, and the combination is quietly impressive.

Depth has a shadow. Scorpio can become secretive, holding back information as a form of control, or testing people to see whether they can be trusted. Hurt rarely evaporates; it can harden into a grudge that lasts years, and jealousy may show up where it feels exposed. All-or-nothing thinking is common, so a single betrayal may end an entire relationship. Under pressure, the sting comes out as a cutting remark aimed precisely where it will land. Much of this grows from a fear of being vulnerable. When Scorpio feels safe, the guardedness tends to soften noticeably.

sections.heading: Scorpio in love and relationships
paragraphs: Scorpio does not tend to love casually. It is usually looking for a bond that goes all the way down, with emotional honesty, physical closeness and a sense that two people are truly in it together. Scorpio offers intense attention, fierce protectiveness and a willingness to stay with a partner through the difficult chapters. It often needs trust above everything else, along with privacy, loyalty that is shown rather than just promised, and a partner who will not flinch when things get heavy. Shallow flirtation or vagueness about commitment can make it withdraw quickly.

The friction points are usually trust and power. A Scorpio who feels uncertain may probe, check or keep part of itself hidden, and partners can experience this as suspicion. Arguments can become a quiet struggle over who has the upper hand. What helps is consistency: doing what you said you would do, answering questions directly, and being open about feelings before Scorpio has to dig for them. Scorpio in turn benefits from voicing fears early rather than testing for them, and from letting a repaired hurt actually stay repaired instead of filing it away for later.

sections.heading: Scorpio at work
paragraphs: At work Scorpio is often the strategist in the corner who has already spotted the weak point in the plan. It is comfortable with complexity, confidentiality and high stakes, which suits research-heavy and investigative roles: detective work, auditing, psychology, surgery, crisis management, forensic accounting, insurance, investing or any field that rewards getting to the bottom of things. As a leader Scorpio tends to be quiet, intense and very loyal to its team, expecting the same commitment in return. It rarely shows its full hand in negotiations, which can be a real advantage.

The pitfalls are mostly about control and trust. Scorpio may find it hard to delegate, keep important information to itself, or treat office politics as a game of chess when a plain conversation would do. A perceived betrayal by a colleague can sour the whole working relationship. With money, Scorpio is often canny and private, good at building reserves and thinking about long-term security, though it can take bold all-in positions when convinced. Writing decisions down, sharing context earlier than feels natural and keeping a trusted second opinion helps a great deal.

sections.heading: Growth and the three Scorpio decans
paragraphs: Growth for Scorpio often means trusting a little before trust has been fully earned, and finding out that the world usually holds. Try sharing one honest feeling a week with someone close, without first checking whether it is safe. When you notice an old grievance replaying, ask what it is protecting you from, and whether that protection is still needed. Letting go is not the same as excusing; it can simply mean that a past hurt stops making today's decisions. Channel the appetite for depth into something that rewards it, such as a demanding craft, a research project or a practice of honest writing. Scorpio's power to transform is real, and it tends to work best when turned inward first.

Scorpio divides into three decans of ten degrees each. The first, roughly October 23 to November 1, belongs to Pluto; the second, about November 2 to November 11, to Neptune; and the third, around November 12 to November 21, to the Moon. Each has its own page, and every Scorpio birthday links to its decan.

faq.question: What is Scorpio's biggest weakness?
faq.answer: The weakness most often named is difficulty letting go. A Scorpio who feels betrayed may hold a grudge, withdraw trust entirely or become controlling to avoid being hurt again. Underneath this is usually a fear of vulnerability, and it tends to ease as Scorpio feels genuinely safe with people.

faq.question: Who is Scorpio most compatible with?
faq.answer: Scorpio is traditionally paired with the other water signs, Cancer and Pisces, which understand emotional depth without explanation. The earth signs Virgo and Capricorn are also described as steady, trustworthy matches. Taurus, its opposite sign, brings strong attraction along with a shared stubborn streak. The full birth chart tells a richer story.

faq.question: What are the dates for Scorpio?
faq.answer: About October 23 to November 21. The Sun's entry into each sign moves by a day or so between years, so birthdays at either end are cusp dates; the zodiac sign calculator settles them for a specific year.

faq.question: What are the three Scorpio decans?
faq.answer: The first decan (0° to 9°) is linked with Pluto, the second (10° to 19°) with Neptune and the third (20° to 29°) with the Moon, following the rulers of the water signs in zodiac order.
